q: The matrix exponential e^A is defined by the power series Σ Aⁿ/n!. For commuting matrices A, B (AB = BA):
exp: For commuting A, B: e^{A+B} = e^A·e^B. Without commutativity, the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formula applies: e^A·e^B = e^{A+B+[A,B]/2+...}. The matrix exponential maps the Lie algebra to the Lie group and is fundamental in solving linear ODEs ẋ = Ax with solution x(t) = e^{At}x₀.
